statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 13% (low) after the fifth observed hour of the CME reopen, in which NQZ26 extended to a fresh 31,221.25 high and then gave back roughly 29 points that remain unrecovered, leaving the contract at 31,192.00, up 0.42% on 27.95k. Stress eases to 60% (elevated) as Brent 101.48 and WTI 90.03 press session lows despite the Strait of Hormuz remaining declared closed, and ZN futures sit 0.13% higher overnight.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. The narrow danger window is drawn across the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and the September ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z, where the published Tail path peaks at 16% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: Tail eases to 13% as the extension to a fresh 31,221.25 high fails and about 29 points stay unrecovered, with narrow leadership and crude at session lows holding Stress to 60%
body:
The reopen is now roughly four and a half hours old and the hour just completed argues for less protection, not more. NQZ26 prints 31,192.00 on Yahoo Finance at 02:16Z and 31,199.25 on Investing.com at 02:16Z, up 130.25 and 137.50 points respectively against a 31,061.75 prior close, a gain of 0.42% to 0.44% on 27.95k contracts. Both independent reads agree on the session high of 31,221.25.

That high is the point. In the prior hour the contract had made 31,203.00, absorbed a 24-point pullback and extended, which is the shallow-pullback-then-extension sequence the contract names as an amplifier. This hour it extended again to 31,221.25, and then the sequence broke: roughly 29 points came off and have not been reabsorbed, leaving price about 22 to 29 points below the high and essentially flat over the hour. An extension that fails and a retracement that holds is the opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks. Tail therefore eases one point to 13%, deep inside the low band, mapping to EA_ON and green, with the dominant mode normal.

Breadth of the move is the second reason for easing. ES prints 7,786.75, up only 0.12% on a 12.25-point range worth 0.16% of index value, against NQ's 0.42%. A 30 basis point divergence between the two headline US index futures is narrow, tech-specific leadership rather than a broad risk-seeking path, and narrow leadership is harder to sustain as a one-way move than a broad one.

What the leadership is made of is visible in Asia. The Nikkei 225 trades 70,026.19, up 2.51% and within 46 points of its 70,072.13 session high, an outright regional melt-up in semiconductor and AI-linked names that still traces back to Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter report of roughly 54.2 billion dollars in revenue and long-term supply commitments rising to 32 billion from 22 billion in June. The relevant observation for this index is that the Nasdaq-100 proxy is emphatically not following Tokyo one-for-one: a 2.51% regional move is producing 0.42% here. That gap is further evidence against treating tonight's drift as the start of a pathological path.

Depth still argues for keeping a premium above a pure floor. Mainland China is closed from 1 to 7 October for National Day and reopens on 8 October, the Korea Stock Exchange is closed on 5 October, and Hong Kong trades without Stock Connect flows in either direction. Price discovery is unusually offshore-driven, which thins the book any extension would have to overcome and raises the chance that a headline in these hours is priced offshore first.

Cross-asset evidence is the reason Stress eases to 60% rather than firming. Iran's parliament speaker has kept the Strait of Hormuz declared closed pending a seven-condition plan, and crude has gone down anyway and gone down further this hour: Brent is 101.48, off 0.75% against a 102.25 prior close with a 101.31 session low, and WTI is 90.03, off 1.19% against 91.11 with an 89.92 low. Both crudes pressing session lows against a declared closure is a clear statement that Gulf risk is not currently transmitting into the index. Reporting on actual flow remains internally contradictory, with transit variously described as a fraction of normal and as running near a 13.5 million barrel per day prewar baseline, so the published assessment leans on the verified price rather than on either flow figure.

The standing constraint is rates. Friday's September payroll report missed at 29,000 against a consensus above 80,000, unemployment rose to 4.2% and average hourly earnings printed 0.1% on the month, yet yields fell and then reversed higher to close up: the 10-year at 5.2939%, the highest in more than two decades, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.78%, 5.24% and 5.61% for the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year as of 1 October. The Nasdaq-100 still closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00%, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31. A record index against a two-decade-high long yield is an expensive and difficult environment, which is what 60% Stress inside the elevated band describes, and it has so far kept mean-reverting. The one piece of live relief tonight is ZN December futures at 104.50, up 0.13%, a marginal bid that eases the yield tension at the edges without resolving it.

Confidence rises one point to 86%. The base added two live cross-asset reads this hour that the previous assessment did not hold: Treasury futures, which are open while cash Treasuries are shut, and a live Nikkei cash print. Those sit alongside two independent verified NQ reads with range and volume, an independent ES read, real-time Brent and WTI, H.15 constant maturities, the complete payroll actuals, the confirmed Asian holiday calendar and a week-ahead US calendar cross-checked against two sources, with the FOMC minutes date verified at 7 October, 2:00 PM Eastern. The deductions that keep Confidence out of the nineties are unchanged: VIX at 15.31 and the 10-year at 5.28 are Friday cash closes rather than live reads, cash Treasuries are shut so the yield tension cannot be confirmed directly, two intended sources returned HTTP 403 bot-blocks so the Hormuz flow strand rests on aggregated reporting, and the shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection time with a partial collection status and two section-level failures, roughly six days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was treated as unavailable and no breadth, megacap or semiconductor cross-check was folded in.

The published path holds Tail at 13% through Tokyo mid-session, where the thin book remains the channel for any unopposed extension, then decays to 12% as the Asian book is assumed to mature into two-way trade. It ticks to 14% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to the 12% floor through the European morning, and rises into the US session: 15% for the 13:00Z hour containing the cash open and the S&P Global finals, and a 16% session peak for the 14:00Z hour carrying September ISM Services at a consensus near 55.0 against a 55.4 August print, whose employment component carries extra weight after a 29,000 payroll gain. Both increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not assertions that opening or post-release continuation has already been observed. The path then decays through the afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, falls to the floor across the 21:00Z maintenance halt, and holds 12% through the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 02:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose to 12% in the 22:00Z slot once the reopen had been observed, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and 15% at 01:00Z on 5 October as the drift extended and a shallow pullback was absorbed. Stress climbed from 75% at 02:00Z to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings into the 14:00Z trough as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and settled at 66%, 65%, 64% and 62% across the four reopen hours. Confidence ran a narrow 83% to 88% band, peaking in the European and early US hours when verified evidence was densest and easing into the thin weekend and reopen hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour recorded a failed extension: NQZ26 made a fresh 31,221.25 high, then gave back roughly 29 points that remain unrecovered, leaving price at 31,192.00, up 0.42%, essentially flat over the hour, while ES managed only 0.12%. Tail therefore eases to 13% and Stress to 60% as Brent and WTI press session lows. Tail holds 13% through Tokyo mid-session, where the holiday-thinned book without mainland China and Korea remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to the 12% floor as the Asian session is assumed to mature into two-way trade. It ticks to 14% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to 12% through the European morning, and rises to 15% and a 16% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the US cash open, the S&P Global services and composite finals and September ISM Services. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances rather than observed structure. The path decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to the floor across the 21:00Z maintenance halt, and holds 12% across the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour remains in the low band and maps to EA_ON, with Stress tracking a 58% to 65% range and Confidence an 83% to 86% range.
